meta.note: Architectural colours from the 1906 excavators' observations on Aphaia (Furtwängler et al. 1906, pp. 30, 35, 46-49); sculpture after Gods in Color; sanctuary materials after the Ministry on-site boards (reference only). Hex values are rendering choices; confidence describes the evidence for the colour, not the exact hue. verified:true = the colour statement was read in the source. `patterns` holds the ornament tile colours.

marble.note: Generic unpainted marble (tiles, sima ground, sculpture plinths).

step-limestone.note: Steps and peristasis floor unpainted, no stucco: natural yellowish-grey limestone (p. 46).

shaft-stucco.note: Fine stucco coat attested; its colour 'nicht mehr zu ermitteln', most probably yellowish like the stone (p. 46).

capital-stucco.note: Thin stucco attested; Garnier saw a dark brown-yellow tone; no ornament found on capitals (p. 46).

architrave.note: Conflict: Garnier red (doubted by the 1906 authors), Klenze yellowish ground (p. 47).

regula.note: Not seen on the peristasis; 1906 authors conjecture black; Cockerell blue from an opisthodomos fragment (p. 47).

triglyph-black.note: Two fragments with distinct black; Cockerell's blue rejected (p. 47).

mutule-black.note: Black directly on stone, no stucco ground; 32 consistent splinters (p. 47).

cornice-soffit-red.note: Viae and underside red, applied directly on stone (p. 47).

cornice-hawksbeak.note: Flank cornice cymatium: red and blue leaves, outlines lightly incised, ornament axes about 5.2 cm (p. 47).

raking-cymatium.note: Cymatium under the raking cornice: blue and red, axes about 19.5 cm (p. 48). Leaf form assumed.

raking-corona-soffit.note: Underside of the raking corona probably red (p. 48).

metope.note: Metopes never found; a thin inserted slab, probably painted wood (pp. 28-29). Colour unknown.

sima-palmette.note: One fragment keeps a definite red; blue-and-red palmettes by Athenian analogy; Cockerell's gilding rejected (p. 48).

antefix-palmette.note: Anthemia visible as smooth patches; probably coloured (pp. 46, 48).

acroterion.note: Colour undeterminable; Klenze saw clear red traces on the ridge acroteria (p. 48, footnote).

cella-wall-dado-red.note: Red behind the door (Garnier, Klenze): perhaps red to about 1 m (p. 48).

cella-wall-upper.note: Light wall above the red dado (p. 48).

interior-crown-meander.note: Interior crowning band seen only by Cockerell and Haller, colours differ; the meander Blouet drew belongs here, not on the corona (pp. 47, 49).

archer-diamond-pattern.note: West-pediment archer: shirt and leggings with a red, yellow, blue and green diamond pattern (layout attested by UV and raking light; exact pigments by analogy). Tile colours in patterns.diamond.

archer-vest-yellow.note: Bright yellow vest with lions and griffins; tall yellow hat with a flower pattern.

rubble-stone.note: Natural-stone socle of the terrace/enclosure wall (Ministry board): local limestone tone, conjectural.

older-masonry.note: Older (mid-6th-c.) masonry of the east stretch, a different technique on the Ministry board (p. 86): darker weathered limestone, conjectural.

mudbrick.note: Mudbrick superstructure (Ziegelaufbau) of the enclosure wall (Ministry board). Unplastered sun-dried clay tone: conjectural.

wall-coping.note: Coping on the mudbrick enclosure wall (Ministry board shows a coping); terracotta tiles assumed, colour conjectural.

ashlar-wall.note: Tall ashlar retaining wall at the NE corner (Ministry board): dressed local limestone, colour conjectural.

rock-face.note: Exposed bedrock faces (NE knoll cave face, cut faces where today's ground rises above the terrace). Limestone tone, conjectural.

house-stucco.note: Priests' houses and other sanctuary buildings: plastered walls assumed, light earth tone, conjectural.

roof-tile-terracotta.note: Hipped tiled roofs of the priests' houses (Ministry board); fired-clay tiles assumed (the temple itself has marble tiles, p. 31).

timber.note: Timber porches, posts and gallery beams: oiled wood tone, conjectural.

pavement.note: Paved altar court and paved way to the ramp (Ministry board legend 5 and 7; two courses of slabs, p. 25). Stone colour itself conjectural.

figure-hair.note: Stand-in figure hair and helmet crests.

figure-shield.note: Stand-in shields (red ground); Gods in Color reconstructions show painted shields, devices omitted.

athena-aegis.note: Athena's garment on the stand-in: a light peplos (with a blue-and-red aegis on the Gods in Color reconstructions, not modelled), kept light so the figure reads against the blue tympanum. Conjectural.

hawksbeak.note: Cymatia of the flank cornice and under the raking cornice: red and blue leaves with lightly incised outlines (pp. 47-48). The leaf form is assumed; ground left as white stucco.

palmette.note: Sima palmettes: one fragment keeps a definite red; blue-and-red palmettes by Athenian analogy (p. 48).

meander.note: Interior crowning band: the meander Blouet drew belongs to the interior crowning blocks; Cockerell and Haller differ on colours (pp. 47, 49).

diamond.note: Archer's shirt and leggings: an intricate red, yellow, blue and green diamond pattern (Harvard Gazette 2007, read). Layout attested on the original by UV and raking light; exact pigments by analogy.
